memory_candidates.content: state-write.sh's --audit-verdict parses the verdict file via `jq --argjson` passed as a shell argument, not --slurpfile; a full audit-task-proposals.sh NDJSON (100KB+) will hit the shell argument-length limit ('Argument list too long'). Workaround: trim the verdict file to the matching proposal plus its non-scope-blind verdicts only (a few KB) before passing it -- the audit-evidence gate only requires a verdict object whose .proposal.id matches the new entry's project_name, not the full verdict set. Commit the full, untrimmed NDJSON separately as the evidence record.

The plan-verification idiom 'git diff --stat <this task's first commit>^..HEAD -- <paths>' is unreliable in a shared working tree where sibling tasks commit concurrently: the window-wide diff captures every writer's commits during that span, not just this task's own. The correct per-task check is to inspect each of the task's own phase commits individually (git show --stat <commit> -- <paths>), confirmed empty for all of them.
